db85827051a7: Ask the student what they did yesterday evening and listen to which forms they use about themselves. This is a diagnostic: we see which conjugations are already solid.
b2db28dce350: I'm reading a book right now.
af8a9f32cd75: Stress this: Polish has no separate continuous tense the way English does. Ask the student for one sentence about «right now» and one about «every Saturday».
c7ccd98b4625: Reveal it row by row and ask the student to say the form aloud. The key is the pair “ja -m / ty -sz”: it tells us which group we are in.
2a969d4c1249: The key here is -ować → -uję. Name three more verbs in -ować (trenować, rysować, fotografować) and ask the learner to form the «ja» form.
10bfadcfee37: Compare with group 2: «ja» is the same (-ę), the difference shows from «ty». So always check two forms: ja and ty.
0951d8eaaa02: Say 5–6 infinitives (pływać, trenować, lubić, słuchać, uczyć się, rysować); the student names the group and the «ja» form. Do not promise that the rule always works.
637f9c1bf286: This is the format of the first listening task in the state exam: a short utterance — where could you hear it. In the exam the recording is played once, so we train catching key words instead of translating everything.
5edcd4081a07: The student makes one sentence about themselves with each word. Stop separately on «nigdy nie» — English uses a single negative («I never go»), so the extra nie is easy to drop.
0d64f37be1dc: pisać and pić look like group 1 or 3, but they conjugate like group 2. In jeździć and chodzić the stem change appears only in the «ja» and «oni» forms.
3a01f2ca2c91: jeść and wiedzieć look like group 1, but «oni» is different. móc is there to contrast with umieć (English “can” covers both) — have the student say all the forms aloud.
c25450939b06: Read the English phrase and give the student a second to say it in Polish before you reveal ✓. Students make these three mistakes most often when talking about hobbies.
0d185f7aa6d1: I can (= I know how to) play the guitar
87bdf2b56837: The last trap continues slide s10. Ask the student what they know how to do (umieć) and what they are able to do today (móc).
